analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a paragraph at head lines ~920-926 about how fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json is regenerated. The file is regenerated in darkbloom-platform at an explicit revision and copied byte-for-byte into this repo. The source revision and SHA-256 are recorded in the commit. A provider prompt-rendering change, such as the Qwen JSON response_format thinking default, must land with regenerated vectors and pass scripts/verify-prompt-parity.sh. I examined both base text units (lines 1-474 and 475-945) against the threat model. The change touches no code, keys, attestation, authorization, cache storage (T-041), WebSocket (TB-002) or App Attest (TB-011) behavior. It introduces no new attack surface. If anything it reinforces the integrity of the fixture provenance by requiring an explicit revision, a hash record and a parity check, and by keeping the public CI from cloning a moving private branch. The remaining unverified contracts are outside the supplied evidence: the content of the regenerated vectors, whether verify-prompt-parity.sh enforces the byte-for-byte match, and the platform sidecar's behavior. These are process claims, not security regressions. The threat model needs no update.
